messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - Dedicated pool 'eclipse-prod-vpc' (tenant: Eclipse Corp) reporting GPU capacity exhaustion in eu-west-1. New requests are queueing. Errors rising. Paging @tim_oncall @aisha_ng. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/dedicated-gpu-exhaustion

Tim_oncall: I'm on it, joining now. What's the immediate user impact?

lia_platform: Dashboard snapshot: 95th token latency jumped 900ms -> 3s. 5xx rate for Eclipse routes +7% over baseline. GPU queue length >120 per node pool.

marc_sre: Confirmed from infra metrics. autoscaler didn't add nodes - tenant is pinned to 8 gpus (max=8) and burst is disabled in config. Queue backlog growing on frontend pods; KV cache pressure low.

aisha_ng: Right — Eclipse is on a reserved dedicated plan that requires manual burst approval. We need explicit customer consent to expand. Carla, can you contact the customer for emergency burst approval? @carla_se

carla_se: Reached out via the customer Slack integration and email, they replied: "approve +4 GPUs for 45m emergency burst, we need service restored". They also asked for a short postmortem.

Tim_oncall: Ok approving emergency burst. Executing control-plane command now.

Tim_oncall: ```
# control-plane CLI
redwoodctl allocate-burst --tenant eclipse --region eu-west-1 --gpus 4 --duration 45m --reason "emergency restore - queue overflow"
```

lia_platform: Allocation accepted by control plane, provisioning started. New instances expected in ~4-7 minutes. Initiating soft-drain of low-priority batch tasks in the pool to free GPU slots faster.

marc_sre: Drain plan: label selector batch=true, preemptible=true. Running eviction script to stop non-customer workloads only (do NOT touch customer-inference pods).

marc_sre: ```
# internal drain (run by platform team)
for node in $(redwoodctl list-nodes --pool eclipse-prod-vpc --status busy); do
  redwoodctl cordon $node
  redwoodctl evict --selector "workload=batch" --node $node
done
```

aisha_ng: Executing now. Evictions in progress, most batch jobs are being rescheduled to tenant-shared preemptible fleet. Monitoring queue length.

customer-relay-bot: Eclipse Corp: "Thanks, we see errors drop on our side — keep us posted."

lia_platform: New capacity came online, pool +4 gpus active. Queue length down from 120 -> 12 in ~5m. 5xxs trending back to baseline.

Tim_oncall: Customer impact window: approx 12:34 - 12:40 UTC for spike; failures intermittent until burst fully active. Please add this to the timeline. :thumbsup:

marc_sre: Post-action checklist: 1) Validate autoscaler policy for pinned tenants 2) Enable emergency-burst bypass for approved contacts 3) Add alert to trigger earlier at queue>50 for dedicated pools. Opening tickets now.

Tim_oncall: Creating incident channel #incident-eclipse-1774042021 and a brief timeline for SRE/PE follow-ups. I will start an initial incident report.

lia_platform: Quick status: CPU/GPU metrics normalizing, latency 95th back under 1s, error rate recovered. Keep monitoring for 30m before closing.

aisha_ng: Taking handoff for day shift, I'll monitor and coordinate the customer postmortem. TL;DR: burst approved by customer, applied via redwoodctl, drained batch tasks, service restored. Follow-ups: autoscaler fallback, alert tuning, document emergency-cc.

Tim_oncall: Thanks team — going offline. Handoff to @aisha_ng. Closing active pager.

incidents-bot: Note: incident created and assigned. Severity: P2. Follow-up tickets linked: RW-3812 (autoscaler fallback), RW-3813 (alert tuning), RW-3814 (postmortem).
